flags.title: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) / Cardiac Emergency
flags.triggerEvidence: Severe crushing chest pain radiating to left arm & jaw with sweating
flags.rationale: Crushing retrosternal chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw with diaphoresis is a classic hallmark of acute myocardial infarction.
flags.actionRequired: Immediate ECG (12-Lead) within 10 minutes, STAT Troponin I, Vitals & Immediate Cardiac Resuscitation Bed

flags.title: Associated Acute Breathlessness
flags.rationale: Secondary respiratory compromise due to acute cardiac pump strain.
flags.actionRequired: High flow oxygen and continuous pulse oximetry monitoring.

symptoms.canonicalName: Pain Radiation to Left Arm & Jaw

adaptiveAnswers.question: When did the chest pain start, and was it sudden?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Sudden onset 2 hours ago while sitting at home
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Acute onset indicates vascular event (ACS) rather than gradual musculoskeletal pain.

adaptiveAnswers.question: How would you describe the feeling of the pain?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Heavy pressure / Crushing weight like a stone on chest (ಭಾರವಾದ ಒತ್ತಡ / ಎದೆ ಹಿಂಡಿದಂತೆ)
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Crushing pressure is classic for ischemic myocardial necrosis.

adaptiveAnswers.question: Does the pain travel anywhere else?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Yes, radiates intensely into left arm and jaw
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Dermatomal C8-T1 nerve root referral characteristic of cardiac origin.

adaptiveAnswers.question: Does the pain increase with physical movement?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Gets much worse with any movement; patient cannot walk
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Ischemia exacerbated by increased myocardial oxygen demand.

adaptiveAnswers.question: Are you experiencing sweating or breathlessness?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Profuse cold sweat, shortness of breath, and feeling faint
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Sympathetic surge and hemodynamic instability warning sign.

flags.title: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Suspected Acute Appendicitis
flags.triggerEvidence: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and intractable vomiting
flags.rationale: Peritoneal irritation in right iliac fossa (McBurney's point) with systemic inflammatory markers requires surgical assessment to rule out appendicular perforation.
flags.actionRequired: Surgical consultation, Abdominal Ultrasonography (USG), Complete Blood Count (CBC) STAT

modifiers: Started around navel, migrated to right lower quadrant

adaptiveAnswers.question: Where in your abdomen is the pain strongest?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Right lower side of belly (ಬಲ ಕೆಳಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ)
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Classic migration of visceral periumbilical pain to somatic parietal peritoneum at McBurney's point.

adaptiveAnswers.question: Is the pain continuous and steady?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Severe, continuous, and worsening with every hour
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Continuous severe pain indicates progressive localized peritonitis.

adaptiveAnswers.question: Do you have vomiting or fever?
adaptiveAnswers.answer: Repeated vomiting twice this morning, cannot eat food
adaptiveAnswers.rationale: Reflex autonomic vomiting associated with acute visceral inflammation.
